summary: Casanare department stands under the national framework of Colombia, and the sources record no departmental legal regime, no departmental enforcement practice and no Casanare-specific incident of violence, discrimination or official hostility toward trans people. The Wikipedia entry for the department itself yields no usable finding. A trans visitor to Casanare therefore faces the national assessment carried by the parent record, with nothing in the departmental sources to raise or lower it.
tangentialFactors:
The armed-group "social cleansing" campaigns that the sources document are recorded in other departments: Caquetá, where flyers and WhatsApp messages named gay and trans people as legitimate military targets and a trans woman candidate was given a week to leave town, and Guajira, where kill lists have circulated since March 2024. No equivalent campaign is sourced for Casanare, and the absence of a Casanare finding is not evidence that none exists.

National killing figures cited in the sources, including eight trans women killed between February and April 2024 and 41 in 2023, are country-wide totals with no departmental breakdown, so they cannot be read as a Casanare rate.
localsOnly: No resident-facing fact specific to Casanare is sourced: the departmental entry records no local ordinance, no departmental police or health practice, and no local institution dealing with gender identity matters. Resident-facing protections and procedures are those of the national framework described in the parent record.
outOfScopeNotes:
Whether armed groups operate in Casanare, and whether trans residents there face the work restrictions reported elsewhere (discrimination limiting trans women to hairdressing or sex work), is unresolved in the sources; neither is documented for this department either way.

No per-department data on killings, complaints or legal gender recognition filings is available in the inventory, so any Casanare-specific comparison with other Colombian departments cannot be sourced and is left unresolved.
